title: Trump’s appearance at Georgia rally disrupted by anti-ICE protesters – US politics live
text: 16.57 EDT Trump Georgia rally disrupted by protesters Donald Trump’s speech to a small crowd of supporters in Dalton, Georgia, was just disrupted by protesters holding up signs against Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE), who were forced out of the crowd by Trump supporters, including a man wearing a yellow Gadsden flag as a cape. Two of the signs denounced the idea of sending ICE officer to the polls on election day, which the administration has refused to rule out. After he began speaking again, Trump praised “the woman in the yellow cape”. “She went up there, ripped them out of their seats and threw them the hell out of here. Where’s the woman with the yellow cape, then? She was great,” Trump said. Protesters hold up signs against ICE before being ejected from Trump’s campaign rally in Dalton, Georgia on Friday. author: Boris Rozhin

text: Знаменитый пёс Папай вернулся на СВО после тяжёлого ранения и снова спас российских солдат от вражеского дрона. Как стало известно SHOT, на днях на одном из направлений наши бойцы попали под очередную атаку украинских БПЛА: их УАЗ сгорел дотла. Экипаж успел выпрыгнуть только благодаря псу Папаю — во время движения он вдруг начал бешено лаять, и солдаты поняли, что приближается опасность. «Мы могли проскочить, но на трассе были колонны гражданских. Начали стрелять, чтобы не допустить попадания в мирные машины. Сбили дрон, но нашу «буханку» сожгли — сами еле успели выпрыгнуть. Папай тоже жив», — рассказал боец с позывным Абрек. Ранее SHOT уже писал о Папае — с самого начала СВО он входил в состав экипажа БМП, считался полноправным членом команды и постоянно передвигался верхом на гусеничной и колёсной технике. К Абреку пёс попал после тяжёлого ранения — животному восстановили сломанную лапу и достали осколки из груди. До и после ранения Папай уже не раз спасал людей своей чуткостью: ребята из подразделения очень благодарны собакену. @shot_shot
author: Boris Rozhin

text: 📆 Еженедельная авторская колонка; ⚡️ Руководителя проекта «Курсы тактической медицины» с позывным «Латыш » ✅ Специально для канала Colonelcassad Прекардиальный удар, представляющий собой нанесение резкого удара кулаком в область нижней трети грудины, долгое время рассматривался в качестве потенциального метода экстренного восстановления эффективного сердечного ритма при внезапной остановке кровообращения, обусловленной желудочковой тахикардией или фибрилляцией желудочков. Однако накопленный клинический опыт и результаты многочисленных исследований за последние десятилетия убедительно продемонстрировали крайне низкую эффективность этого метода и наличие значительных рисков, что привело к его исключению из большинства современных протоколов сердечно-легочной реанимации. Согласно данным, обобщенным в ведущих клинических руководствах, частота успешного восстановления ритма после прекардиального удара не превышает долей процента, что делает его клинически незначимым вмешательством. Основная опасность заключается не только в его бесполезности, но и в отсрочке начала базовой реанимации. Попытка нанести удар отнимает драгоценные секунды, которые должны быть использованы для начала непрямог

text: КГБ рассуждает про воздушные дроны в 1989 году, а немцы гоняют наземный FPV в 1944-м. Смотришь на такое - и диву даёшься: все давно придумано. Вот только почему не применялось? А ответ как раз и даёт статья из журнала «Труды высшей школы КГБ» : дяденьки пытаются осмыслить это сугубо в своём узком поле зрения. Связь с зафронтовыми агентами, радиорелейные передатчики какие-то, мутные специальные задачи. В итоге дрон получался элитарным изделием, штучным продуктом, который создавался в рамках гигантских оборонных бюджетов сверхдержав для стратегической разведки. А революцию совершили не военные, а гражданский рынок . Смартфонный бум 2010-х годов сделал микросхемы, литиевые аккумуляторы, гироскопы и камеры микроскопическими и дешевыми, появилась спутниковая навигация и прочие штуки. То есть, возможность пересобрать всё базе дешевых гражданских технологий. Вот лучшее доказательство того, что гениальная инженерная идея ничего не значит без развитой и дешевой массовой индустрии. Потому, что идти надо всегда от потребностей нормальной жизни, а не от способов кого-то убить. Соответственно, и сейчас выключи режим войны - и куда девать многочисленные разработки? Гражданской индустрии в воюющи
author: Boris Rozhin

text: Черт меня дёрнул, и я решил посмотреть зеленского у Пирса Моргана полностью. Про то, как президент Украины тянет слова, шмыгает носом и наклонив голову странно смотрит на Пирса, оставлю за скобками. Далее конспектирую по смыслу, чтоб потом не забыть. - говорит, что для украинцев это война за себя, но для кого-то (американцев по смыслу) это экономика и бизнесс. Добавляет после паузы, что это обидно. Я так понимаю это, что теории роста украинского благосостояния от войны как-то отошли на второй план? Собирались же запанувать во всем мире и торговать оружием задорого, ещё и план маршала получить. - Трамп плохой, Маск плохой, энергетическое перемирие плохо, но мы были готовы, чтобы народ пережил зиму. А их кинули, так ещё и старлинк отключили . Ну так не надо было начинать летом план очередной перемоги. И ещё проблема в догонку, что прекращения огня благодаря Украине, никогда не работали. - Старлинк не для нападения. Частично он для мидл-страйка, и, конечно, они (американцы) блокировал мидл-страйки. Но они надавили: предупреждение о баллистических ударах не дали, а потом отключили старлинки. Ну тут мне и почти нечего добавить. Оказывается все украинские технологии от мидл-страйка до ун

text: Прямо сейчас в Санкт-Петербурге спецназ и оперативники ведут проверку соблюдения миграционного законодательства среди иностранных граждан на Сенном рынке, в том числе собравшихся на пятничную молитву. Также в проверке участвуют представители военкоматов, которые оценивают своевременность постановки на воинский учет граждан, недавнем прошлом получивших паспорта Российской Федерации. К текущему моменту выявлено несколько десятков человек, которым вручены повестки для прибытия в военкомат в целях постановки на воинский учет. По полученной информации несколько сотен правоохранителей оцепили квартал на Московском проспекте неподалеку от Сенного рынка, где расположено молельное помещение, количество прихожан в котором достигает тысячи человек. Правоохранители также проверяют деятельность молельного помещения на предмет его соответствия законодательству РФ в сфере обрядовой деятельности и многочисленных хостелов и этнических кафе, расположенных в соседних зданиях, где проживают мигранты. По имеющимся данным в настоящее время в результате проверочных мероприятий уже задержано несколько десятков прихожан, имеющих при себе миграционные документы, оформленные с нарушением законодательства РФ.
author: Boris Rozhin

title: Trump denies limiting Ukraine access to Starlink network
text: Trump denies limiting Ukraine access to Starlink network Image source, Getty Images By Hafsa Khalil Published 4 hours ago US President Donald Trump has denied limiting Ukraine's access to Starlink's sister internet network Starshield after it restricted drone speed, hampering Kyiv's ability to protect itself from Russian attacks. "It wasn't me and I don't think it was [Starlink owner] Elon [Musk]," Trump said, hours after Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said speed had yet to be restored. Musk himself suggested the US government might have been behind the restrictions, while Reuters news agency reported on Thursday that the order had come from inside the White House. Ukraine was hit by several deadly strikes on Tuesday after the network slowdown. Starlink is a civilian-use high-speed internet network operated by Musk's SpaceX. Starshield - which relies on Starlink- is its military-grade sister service that was designed for the Pentagon. The US had previously warned it could withhold sharing intelligence, crucial for Kyiv's defences, if Ukraine did not stop hitting Russian oil refineries. text: Watch: BBC follows Ukraine's Operation Vivaldi pushing Russia back on frontline Watch: BBC follows Ukraine's Operation Vivaldi pushing Russia back on frontline Close Deep inside an underground bunker in eastern Ukraine, commanders monitor the battlefield through a live video feed as a Ukrainian drone intercepts a Russian surveillance drone. While Russian firms stand to benefit from looser export restrictions, the promised shipments may do little to bring down U.S. fuel prices. The agreement has drawn scathing criticism from Ukraine and its European allies, as well as scrutiny from lawmakers at home. But does it make economic sense? What does Trump want? Trump announced that Russia would “immediately” supply 300,000 tons of diesel to the U.S. and global markets, followed by another 500,000 metric tons in November and 1 million metric tons thereafter. The deal comes as U.S. diesel prices have risen to $6.179 per gallon, up nearly 70% year-on-year, amid the turmoil that has gripped the global oil market since the start of the Iran war in late February. text: St. Petersburg Bans Migrant Workers From Gym, Hair Salon and Retail Work Oct. 16, 2026 Igor Ivanko / Moskva News Agency St. Petersburg authorities have banned foreign citizens with work patents from employment in retail, healthcare, beauty salons and fitness centers, local media reported Thursday. Governor Alexander Beglov’s decree expands on existing restrictions, which last year banned migrant patent holders — a temporary low-skilled work visa — from driving taxis and delivering food. Employers have been given until Dec. 15 to bring their staffing into compliance. The decision aims to combat “shadow employment” and reduce economic reliance on low-skilled foreign labor, according to local outlet Fontanka. According to St. Petersburg authorities, it will also facilitate “a transparent, regulated labor market where jobs are generated for Russian citizens, including young people and students.” The restrictions do not apply to highly qualified specialists, foreigners with work permits or citizens of Armenia, Belarus, Kazakhstan or Kyrgyzstan. title: Trump denies limiting Ukraine access to Starlink network
text: Trump denies limiting Ukraine access to Starlink network Image source, Getty Images By Hafsa Khalil Published 16 October 2026 US President Donald Trump has denied limiting Ukraine's access to Starlink's sister internet network Starshield after it restricted drone speed, hampering Kyiv's ability to protect itself from Russian attacks. "It wasn't me and I don't think it was [Starlink owner] Elon [Musk]," Trump said, hours after Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said the usual speed had yet to be restored. Musk himself suggested the US government might have been behind the restrictions, while news agency Reuters reported on Thursday that the order had come from inside the White House. Ukraine was hit by several deadly strikes on Tuesday after the network slowdown. Starlink is a civilian-use, high-speed internet network operated by Musk's SpaceX. Starshield - which relies on Starlink - is its military-grade counterpart that was designed for the Pentagon. The US had previously warned it could withhold sharing intelligence, crucial for Kyiv's defences, if Ukraine did not stop hitting Russian oil refineries. title: Watch: BBC follows Ukraine's Operation Vivaldi pushing Russia back on frontline
text: Watch: BBC follows Ukraine's Operation Vivaldi pushing Russia back on frontline Watch: BBC follows Ukraine's Operation Vivaldi pushing Russia back on frontline Close Deep inside an underground bunker in eastern Ukraine, commanders monitor the battlefield through a live video feed as a Ukrainian drone intercepts a Russian surveillance drone. text: US senators call for investigation into Ukraine's Starlink restrictions Image source, Getty Images Image caption, Democratic Party Senator Jeanne Shaheen has spearheaded the cross-party statement from several US senators By Jack Burgess Published 16 October 2026 A bipartisan group of US senators has signed a letter demanding an urgent investigation into disruptions to SpaceX's Starlink internet network in Ukraine. text: St. Petersburg Bans Migrant Workers From Gym, Hair Salon and Retail Work Oct. 16, 2026 Igor Ivanko / Moskva News Agency St. Petersburg authorities have banned foreign citizens with work patents from employment in retail, healthcare, beauty salons and fitness centers, local media reported Thursday. Governor Alexander Beglov’s decree expands on existing restrictions, which last year banned migrant patent holders — a temporary low-skilled work visa — from driving taxis and delivering food. Employers have been given until Dec. 15 to bring their staffing into compliance. text: Ukrainian Drones Strike Energy Plant in Russia’s Largest Oil-Producing Region Oct. 16, 2026 @exilenova_plus / Telegram A suspected Ukrainian drone attack sparked a fire at an industrial facility in western Siberia’s Khanty-Mansi autonomous district on Friday, local authorities said, in what appeared to be the first strike on energy infrastructure in Russia’s largest oil-producing region. Governor Ruslan Kukharuk said an “industrial facility in the Surgut district” caught fire following the attack. The extent of the damage was still being assessed. Residents identified the facility as the Surgut Condensate Stabilization Plant, according to the Ukrainian monitoring channel Supernova+ . Eyewitness footage shared by the channel showed a large fire sending thick black smoke into the sky. The plant, owned by Gazprom Pererabotka, is Russia’s largest facility for processing a mixture of crude oil and gas condensate, with a design capacity of 12 million metric tons per year. It produces gasoline, diesel, jet fuel, liquefied petroleum gas and stabilized gas condensate. Surgut lies around 2,500 kilometers (1,550 miles) from the Ukrainian border. title: Jailed Election Expert Kynev Denied Crutches After Leg Broken During Arrest, Journalist Says
text: Jailed Election Expert Kynev Denied Crutches After Leg Broken During Arrest, Journalist Says Oct. 16, 2026 Alexander Kynev. Vayvor Russian political scientist and election expert Alexander Kynev is unable to walk after being denied crutches at a Moscow detention center, a journalist who received a letter from him said. Kynev, who was arrested in late September on drug charges, has been transferred to Moscow’s Pre-Trial Detention Center No. 4, known as “Medved” (“Bear”), journalist Gleb Yarovoy said . His leg was reportedly broken during his arrest. “He writes that he is still in a cast and has about three more weeks to ‘walk’ around in it. Except he can’t walk,” Yarovoy wrote. Kynev also said he was being held in quarantine and receiving no information about the outside world, according to Yarovoy. Moscow’s Perovsky District Court ordered Kynev into pre-trial detention on Sept. 25 on charges of attempting to sell a large quantity of drugs. He denies wrongdoing and faces between 10 and 20 years in prison if convicted. title: Putin Hands Control of 5 Western Firms to Ukraine War Veteran
text: Putin Hands Control of 5 Western Firms to Ukraine War Veteran Oct. 16, 2026 Marat Mirkhaidarov. Social media President Vladimir Putin signed a decree Thursday placing the Russian assets of five major Western manufacturing companies under the temporary management of a little-known firm owned by an ex-official who fought in Ukraine. The targeted European and U.S. assets include French flooring giant Tarkett, Belgian hygiene manufacturer Ontex Ru, German plastic packager Menshen, corrugated producer Kappa Rus and metal packaging producer Eviosys, a subsidiary of the U.S. Sonoco Products Company. Their combined 2025 revenue exceeds 53 billion rubles ($633.2 million), with Tarkett accounting for 19.3 billion rubles, Kappa Rus 16.5 billion rubles, Ontex Ru 10.3 billion rubles, and Eviosys and Menshen 6.1 billion rubles and 1.4 billion rubles, respectively. Putin’s decree hands management rights to Tsentr Kapital Management Company, a Moscow entity established in February 2026, according to corporate registry data cited by RBC. text: Russia Repels 644 Ukrainian Drones as Trump Calls Attacks on Russian Refineries ‘Disgrace’ Oct. 16, 2026 Moscow Sheremetyevo Airport. title: Order to restrict Starlink’s operations in Ukraine came from White House, Reuters reports
text: SpaceX restricted the operation of the military version of Starlink in Ukraine on orders from the White House, Reuters reported, citing unnamed sources. The sources did not specify who issued the order. One senior official told Reuters the order did not come from the U.S. president but did not provide further details. Ukrainian officials and military began reporting problems with Starshield — the military version of Starlink — on the morning of October 14, amid a crisis in relations between U.S. President Donald Trump and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky. Ukrainian military officials said some missions were disrupted because of the restrictions. SpaceX head Elon Musk announced that the Starshield systems are owned and controlled by U.S. authorities. The White House has not officially announced restrictions on Starlink in Ukraine. Sources who spoke to Axios insisted that the U.S. president’s administration has nothing to do with the restrictions. On the morning of October 15, Ukrainian media, citing military officials, reported that Starshield’s operations for the Ukrainian armed forces had fully resumed. text: St. Petersburg Bans Migrant Workers From Gym, Hair Salon and Retail Work Oct. 16, 2026 Igor Ivanko / Moskva News Agency St. Petersburg authorities have banned foreign citizens with work patents from employment in retail, healthcare, beauty salons and fitness centers, local media reported Thursday. Governor Alexander Beglov’s decree expands on existing restrictions, which last year banned migrant patent holders — a temporary low-skilled work visa — from driving taxis and delivering food. Employers have been given until Dec. 15 to bring their staffing into compliance. The decision aims to combat “shadow employment” and reduce economic reliance on low-skilled foreign labor, according to local outlet Fontanka. According to St. Petersburg authorities, it will also facilitate “a transparent, regulated labor market where jobs are generated for Russian citizens, including young people and students.” The restrictions do not apply to highly qualified specialists, foreigners with work permits or citizens of Armenia, Belarus, Kazakhstan or Kyrgyzstan. Nearly 160 flights were delayed or canceled across Moscow’s four main airports, with Sheremetyevo and Vnukovo bearing the brunt. title: Trump denies limiting Ukraine access to Starlink network
text: Trump denies limiting Ukraine access to Starlink network Image source, Getty Images By Hafsa Khalil Published 16 October 2026 US President Donald Trump has denied limiting Ukraine's access to Starlink's sister internet network Starshield after it restricted drone speed, hampering Kyiv's ability to protect itself from Russian attacks. "It wasn't me and I don't think it was [Starlink owner] Elon [Musk]," Trump said, hours after Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said the usual speed had yet to be restored. Musk himself suggested the US government might have been behind the restrictions, while news agency Reuters reported on Thursday that the order had come from inside the White House. Ukraine was hit by several deadly strikes on Tuesday after the network slowdown. Starlink is a civilian-use, high-speed internet network operated by Musk's SpaceX. Starshield - which relies on Starlink - is its military-grade counterpart that was designed for the Pentagon. The US had previously warned it could withhold sharing intelligence, crucial for Kyiv's defences, if Ukraine did not stop hitting Russian oil refineries. title: Watch: BBC follows Ukraine's Operation Vivaldi pushing Russia back on frontline
text: Watch: BBC follows Ukraine's Operation Vivaldi pushing Russia back on frontline Watch: BBC follows Ukraine's Operation Vivaldi pushing Russia back on frontline Close Deep inside an underground bunker in eastern Ukraine, commanders monitor the battlefield through a live video feed as a Ukrainian drone intercepts a Russian surveillance drone. The footage shows the Ukrainian drone hovering above its target, before dropping a net and dragging it from the sky. The interception is part of Operation Vivaldi, a Ukrainian counter-offensive that Kyiv says has recaptured 277 sq km (106 square miles) of territory in the eastern Donbas region in recent months. But Ukraine says new restrictions on Starshield, the military version of Elon Musk's Starlink satellite network, are threatening its drone operations. The technology has played a key role in helping Ukrainian forces detect and strike Russian targets. Dan Johnson reports from the bunker. Read more about Ukraine's counter-offensive. title: Inside Ukrainian offensive pushing Russia back - with Starlink playing a key role
text: Inside Ukrainian offensive pushing Russia back - with Starlink playing a key role Figure caption, Watch: BBC follows Ukraine's Operation Vivaldi pushing Russia back on frontline By Dan Johnson Ukraine correspondent ,Â Reporting from near Lyman, eastern Ukraine Published 16 October 2026 A Russian drone zips across the computer screen, startling the commanders keeping watch over the battlefield via a live stream in their bunker. Cigarette in one hand, radio in the other, one of them calls in their own drone to bring it down and warns the soldiers below of the threat. The men are dangerously exposed, on the long walk across open ground from their front line positions. They are being replaced after three months forcing the Russians back. This is part of Operation Vivaldi, a Ukrainian counter-offensive which they say has liberated 277 sq km (106 square miles) in the eastern Donbas region in recent months. The name reflects the offensive's four stages, or seasons - like the Italian composer's violin concerto. title: US senators call for investigation into Ukraine's Starlink restrictions
text: US senators call for investigation into Ukraine's Starlink restrictions Image source, Getty Images Image caption, Democratic Party Senator Jeanne Shaheen has spearheaded the cross-party statement from several US senators By Jack Burgess Published 16 October 2026 A bipartisan group of US senators has signed a letter demanding an urgent investigation into disruptions to SpaceX's Starlink internet network in Ukraine. Starlink is a vital tool allowing Kyiv to guide drones to Russian targets and protect its own skies, but on Tuesday night Ukraine said it had unexpectedly restricted how fast drones could fly while maintaining internet connection. In the letter, sent to the US defence department inspector general, the senators express "grave concern" about reports of speed curbs between 12 and 14 October. Asked whether the US might have had a role in the slowdown, a US official told the BBC "no such request was ever made by the president [Donald Trump]". The letter, led by Jeanne Shaheen - a Democrat on the Senate's Foreign Relations Committee - calls for the inspector general to find out whether the restrictions were caused by the US defence department or its contractors. title: Russian Firms Stand to Gain Most From Trump’s Diesel Deal, Analysts Say
text: News Analysis Russian Firms Stand to Gain Most From Trump’s Diesel Deal, Analysts Say By Moscow Times Reporter Oct. 16, 2026 An employee holds a diesel fuel pump nozzle at a gas station in Moscow. REUTERS / Maxim Shemetov U.S. President Donald Trump’s diesel deal with Moscow could do more for Russian oil companies than for the American consumers he wants to help, analysts say. While Russian firms stand to benefit from looser export restrictions, the promised shipments may do little to bring down U.S. fuel prices. The agreement has drawn scathing criticism from Ukraine and its European allies, as well as scrutiny from lawmakers at home. But does it make economic sense? What does Trump want? Trump announced that Russia would “immediately” supply 300,000 tons of diesel to the U.S. and global markets, followed by another 500,000 metric tons in November and 1 million metric tons thereafter. The deal comes as U.S. diesel prices have risen to $6.179 per gallon, up nearly 70% year-on-year, amid the turmoil that has gripped the global oil market since the start of the Iran war in late February. title: Russian Courts Paralyzed by Yandex Cloud Outages After Drone Attacks – Vyorstka
text: Russian Courts Paralyzed by Yandex Cloud Outages After Drone Attacks – Vyorstka Oct. 16, 2026 Moskva News Agency Russian arbitration courts have been forced to postpone hearings and freeze legal filings following widespread system failures caused by Ukrainian drone attacks on Yandex data centers, exiled outlet Vyorstka reported Friday. The technical disruptions reportedly began on Oct. 8 after a Ukrainian drone attack damaged the first of three Yandex data centers in Russia. According to Vyorstka, the outages disabled online video hearings, froze official audio recordings and prevented judges from opening or downloading case files submitted by the parties. Judges were reportedly forced to put cases on hold, declare trial breaks or leave bankruptcy filings frozen. Court rulings directly cited server failures at Yandex Cloud as the reason for legal proceedings. “Difficulties operating the ‘Electronic Justice’ software package are observed on Oct. 14 due to a massive failure in the Yandex Cloud main data center,” states one judicial order by a regional court shared by the outlet. title: St. Petersburg Bans Migrant Workers From Gym, Hair Salon and Retail Work
text: St. Petersburg Bans Migrant Workers From Gym, Hair Salon and Retail Work Oct. 16, 2026 Igor Ivanko / Moskva News Agency St. Petersburg authorities have banned foreign citizens with work patents from employment in retail, healthcare, beauty salons and fitness centers, local media reported Thursday. Governor Alexander Beglov’s decree expands on existing restrictions, which last year banned migrant patent holders — a temporary low-skilled work visa — from driving taxis and delivering food. Employers have been given until Dec. 15 to bring their staffing into compliance. The decision aims to combat “shadow employment” and reduce economic reliance on low-skilled foreign labor, according to local outlet Fontanka. According to St. Petersburg authorities, it will also facilitate “a transparent, regulated labor market where jobs are generated for Russian citizens, including young people and students.” The restrictions do not apply to highly qualified specialists, foreigners with work permits or citizens of Armenia, Belarus, Kazakhstan or Kyrgyzstan. title: Ukrainian Drones Strike Energy Plant in Russia’s Largest Oil-Producing Region
text: Ukrainian Drones Strike Energy Plant in Russia’s Largest Oil-Producing Region Oct. 16, 2026 @exilenova_plus / Telegram A suspected Ukrainian drone attack sparked a fire at an industrial facility in western Siberia’s Khanty-Mansi autonomous district on Friday, local authorities said, in what appeared to be the first strike on energy infrastructure in Russia’s largest oil-producing region. Governor Ruslan Kukharuk said an “industrial facility in the Surgut district” caught fire following the attack. The extent of the damage was still being assessed. Residents identified the facility as the Surgut Condensate Stabilization Plant, according to the Ukrainian monitoring channel Supernova+ . Eyewitness footage shared by the channel showed a large fire sending thick black smoke into the sky. The plant, owned by Gazprom Pererabotka, is Russia’s largest facility for processing a mixture of crude oil and gas condensate, with a design capacity of 12 million metric tons per year. It produces gasoline, diesel, jet fuel, liquefied petroleum gas and stabilized gas condensate. Surgut lies around 2,500 kilometers (1,550 miles) from the Ukrainian border. title: Jailed Election Expert Kynev Denied Crutches After Leg Broken During Arrest, Journalist Says
text: Jailed Election Expert Kynev Denied Crutches After Leg Broken During Arrest, Journalist Says Oct. 16, 2026 Alexander Kynev. Vayvor Russian political scientist and election expert Alexander Kynev is unable to walk after being denied crutches at a Moscow detention center, a journalist who received a letter from him said. Kynev, who was arrested in late September on drug charges, has been transferred to Moscow’s Pre-Trial Detention Center No. 4, known as “Medved” (“Bear”), journalist Gleb Yarovoy said . His leg was reportedly broken during his arrest. “He writes that he is still in a cast and has about three more weeks to ‘walk’ around in it. Except he can’t walk,” Yarovoy wrote. Kynev also said he was being held in quarantine and receiving no information about the outside world, according to Yarovoy. Moscow’s Perovsky District Court ordered Kynev into pre-trial detention on Sept. 25 on charges of attempting to sell a large quantity of drugs. He denies wrongdoing and faces between 10 and 20 years in prison if convicted. text: Novaya Gazeta Editor-in-Chief Detained in Moscow Oct. 16, 2026 Sergei Sokolov. @tvrain / X Russian law enforcement officers on Thursday raided the Moscow apartment of Sergei Sokolov, the editor-in-chief of independent newspaper Novaya Gazeta, before taking him in for questioning and subsequently releasing him. Novaya Gazeta said contact with Sokolov was initially lost at around noon Moscow time before he was scheduled to lead an editorial planning meeting. The publication said Sokolov was being transported to the Investigative Committee, Russia’s top investigative body, for questioning and that a lawyer was on their way to assist him. Sokolov was later released on Thursday evening after law enforcement questioned him, reportedly in connection with the case against Novaya Gazeta managing editor Oleg Roldugin. The raid on Sokolov’s apartment was conducted as part of an ongoing criminal investigation opened earlier this spring, law enforcement sources told the RBC outlet. title: Putin Hands Control of 5 Western Firms to Ukraine War Veteran
text: Putin Hands Control of 5 Western Firms to Ukraine War Veteran Oct. 16, 2026 Marat Mirkhaidarov. Social media President Vladimir Putin signed a decree Thursday placing the Russian assets of five major Western manufacturing companies under the temporary management of a little-known firm owned by an ex-official who fought in Ukraine. The targeted European and U.S. assets include French flooring giant Tarkett, Belgian hygiene manufacturer Ontex Ru, German plastic packager Menshen, corrugated producer Kappa Rus and metal packaging producer Eviosys, a subsidiary of the U.S. Sonoco Products Company. Their combined 2025 revenue exceeds 53 billion rubles ($633.2 million), with Tarkett accounting for 19.3 billion rubles, Kappa Rus 16.5 billion rubles, Ontex Ru 10.3 billion rubles, and Eviosys and Menshen 6.1 billion rubles and 1.4 billion rubles, respectively. Putin’s decree hands management rights to Tsentr Kapital Management Company, a Moscow entity established in February 2026, according to corporate registry data cited by RBC. title: St. Petersburg Bans Migrant Workers From Gym, Hair Salon and Retail Work
text: St. Petersburg Bans Migrant Workers From Gym, Hair Salon and Retail Work Oct. 16, 2026 Igor Ivanko / Moskva News Agency St. Petersburg authorities have banned foreign citizens with work patents from employment in retail, healthcare, beauty salons and fitness centers, local media reported Thursday. Governor Alexander Beglov’s decree expands on existing restrictions, which last year banned migrant patent holders — a temporary low-skilled work visa — from driving taxis and delivering food. Employers have been given until Dec. 15 to bring their staffing into compliance. The decision aims to combat “shadow employment” and reduce economic reliance on low-skilled foreign labor, according to local outlet Fontanka. According to St. Petersburg authorities, it will also facilitate “a transparent, regulated labor market where jobs are generated for Russian citizens, including young people and students.” The restrictions do not apply to highly qualified specialists, foreigners with work permits or citizens of Armenia, Belarus, Kazakhstan or Kyrgyzstan. title: Putin Vows Retribution for Attacks on Russian Data Centers While Downplaying Damage to Refineries
text: Putin Vows Retribution for Attacks on Russian Data Centers While Downplaying Damage to Refineries Oct. 16, 2026 Sputnik / Mikhail Metzel / Pool via REUTERS President Vladimir Putin warned Thursday that Russia is actively retaliating in response to recent Ukrainian attacks on its data centers, while simultaneously brushing off recent drone attacks on oil refineries. “They took the first step and we began to answer. text: Ukrainian Drones Strike Energy Plant in Russia’s Largest Oil-Producing Region Oct. 16, 2026 @exilenova_plus / Telegram A suspected Ukrainian drone attack sparked a fire at an industrial facility in western Siberia’s Khanty-Mansi autonomous district on Friday, local authorities said, in what appeared to be the first strike on energy infrastructure in Russia’s largest oil-producing region. Governor Ruslan Kukharuk said an “industrial facility in the Surgut district” caught fire following the attack. The extent of the damage was still being assessed. Residents identified the facility as the Surgut Condensate Stabilization Plant, according to the Ukrainian monitoring channel Supernova+ . Eyewitness footage shared by the channel showed a large fire sending thick black smoke into the sky. The plant, owned by Gazprom Pererabotka, is Russia’s largest facility for processing a mixture of crude oil and gas condensate, with a design capacity of 12 million metric tons per year. It produces gasoline, diesel, jet fuel, liquefied petroleum gas and stabilized gas condensate. Surgut lies around 2,500 kilometers (1,550 miles) from the Ukrainian border. title: Jailed Election Expert Kynev Denied Crutches After Leg Broken During Arrest, Journalist Says
text: Jailed Election Expert Kynev Denied Crutches After Leg Broken During Arrest, Journalist Says Oct. 16, 2026 Alexander Kynev. Vayvor Russian political scientist and election expert Alexander Kynev is unable to walk after being denied crutches at a Moscow detention center, a journalist who received a letter from him said. Kynev, who was arrested in late September on drug charges, has been transferred to Moscow’s Pre-Trial Detention Center No. 4, known as “Medved” (“Bear”), journalist Gleb Yarovoy said . His leg was reportedly broken during his arrest. “He writes that he is still in a cast and has about three more weeks to ‘walk’ around in it. Except he can’t walk,” Yarovoy wrote. Kynev also said he was being held in quarantine and receiving no information about the outside world, according to Yarovoy. Moscow’s Perovsky District Court ordered Kynev into pre-trial detention on Sept. 25 on charges of attempting to sell a large quantity of drugs. He denies wrongdoing and faces between 10 and 20 years in prison if convicted. title: Novaya Gazeta Editor-in-Chief Detained in Moscow
text: Novaya Gazeta Editor-in-Chief Detained in Moscow Oct. 16, 2026 Sergei Sokolov. @tvrain / X Russian law enforcement officers on Thursday raided the Moscow apartment of Sergei Sokolov, the editor-in-chief of independent newspaper Novaya Gazeta, before taking him in for questioning and subsequently releasing him. Novaya Gazeta said contact with Sokolov was initially lost at around noon Moscow time before he was scheduled to lead an editorial planning meeting. The publication said Sokolov was being transported to the Investigative Committee, Russia’s top investigative body, for questioning and that a lawyer was on their way to assist him. Sokolov was later released on Thursday evening after law enforcement questioned him, reportedly in connection with the case against Novaya Gazeta managing editor Oleg Roldugin. The raid on Sokolov’s apartment was conducted as part of an ongoing criminal investigation opened earlier this spring, law enforcement sources told the RBC outlet. title: Putin Hands Control of 5 Western Firms to Ukraine War Veteran
text: Putin Hands Control of 5 Western Firms to Ukraine War Veteran Oct. 16, 2026 Marat Mirkhaidarov. Social media President Vladimir Putin signed a decree Thursday placing the Russian assets of five major Western manufacturing companies under the temporary management of a little-known firm owned by an ex-official who fought in Ukraine. The targeted European and U.S. assets include French flooring giant Tarkett, Belgian hygiene manufacturer Ontex Ru, German plastic packager Menshen, corrugated producer Kappa Rus and metal packaging producer Eviosys, a subsidiary of the U.S. Sonoco Products Company. Their combined 2025 revenue exceeds 53 billion rubles ($633.2 million), with Tarkett accounting for 19.3 billion rubles, Kappa Rus 16.5 billion rubles, Ontex Ru 10.3 billion rubles, and Eviosys and Menshen 6.1 billion rubles and 1.4 billion rubles, respectively. Putin’s decree hands management rights to Tsentr Kapital Management Company, a Moscow entity established in February 2026, according to corporate registry data cited by RBC. text: Russia Repels 644 Ukrainian Drones as Trump Calls Attacks on Russian Refineries ‘Disgrace’ Oct. 16, 2026 Moscow Sheremetyevo Airport. text: Trump denies limiting Ukraine access to Starlink network Image source, Getty Images By Hafsa Khalil Published 16 October 2026 US President Donald Trump has denied limiting Ukraine's access to Starlink's sister internet network Starshield after it restricted drone speed, hampering Kyiv's ability to protect itself from Russian attacks. title: Watch: BBC follows Ukraine's Operation Vivaldi pushing Russia back on frontline
text: Watch: BBC follows Ukraine's Operation Vivaldi pushing Russia back on frontline Watch: BBC follows Ukraine's Operation Vivaldi pushing Russia back on frontline Close Deep inside an underground bunker in eastern Ukraine, commanders monitor the battlefield through a live video feed as a Ukrainian drone intercepts a Russian surveillance drone. The footage shows the Ukrainian drone hovering above its target, before dropping a net and dragging it from the sky. The interception is part of Operation Vivaldi, a Ukrainian counter-offensive that Kyiv says has recaptured 277 sq km (106 square miles) of territory in the eastern Donbas region in recent months. But Ukraine says new restrictions on Starshield, the military version of Elon Musk's Starlink satellite network, are threatening its drone operations. The technology has played a key role in helping Ukrainian forces detect and strike Russian targets. Dan Johnson reports from the bunker. Read more about Ukraine's counter-offensive. title: 'US tilting toward Russia: Europeans are standing more and more solidly with Zelensky'
text: As transatlantic relations confront renewed geopolitical uncertainty, former Estonian President Toomas Hendrik Ilves delivers a pointed assessment of Washington's shifting approach to Russia's war on Ukraine and the profound implications for European security. At the heart of his analysis lies a fundamental question: can Europe develop the political unity, strategic independence and military capabilities necessary to defend its interests in an increasingly unpredictable international order? Ilves response: "If there's any time for Europe to begin to act as Europe and not as being strictly self-interested, then this is the time for it."
author: Gavin LEE

title: The risks faced by women migrants in Europe
text: This October marks 10 years since French police dismantled the notorious Calais "Jungle" camp. FRANCE 24's Claire Paccalin returns to the region to explore what has changed for migrants over the past decade. She joins Annette Young and Dr Marissa Quie of Cambridge University to discuss migration routes and their growing role in European political debate.
author: Annette YOUNG

title: UK bookstores scramble as Sally Rooney's novels pulled over Palestine Action support
text: Critically acclaimed Irish novelist Sally Rooney's announcement that her books could no longer be sold in the UK due to her support for proscribed group Palestine Action has left British booksellers rushing to stock up on her works before distributors run out. The British government's ban on the group, which practiced non-violent direct action and sabotage against UK military assets believed to be working with the Israeli government, makes support for Palestine Action punishable by up to 14 years in prison.

title: Russian Firms Stand to Gain Most From Trump’s Diesel Deal, Analysts Say
text: News Analysis Russian Firms Stand to Gain Most From Trump’s Diesel Deal, Analysts Say By Moscow Times Reporter Oct. 16, 2026 An employee holds a diesel fuel pump nozzle at a gas station in Moscow. REUTERS / Maxim Shemetov U.S. President Donald Trump’s diesel deal with Moscow could do more for Russian oil companies than for the American consumers he wants to help, analysts say. While Russian firms stand to benefit from looser export restrictions, the promised shipments may do little to bring down U.S. fuel prices. The agreement has drawn scathing criticism from Ukraine and its European allies, as well as scrutiny from lawmakers at home. But does it make economic sense? What does Trump want? Trump announced that Russia would “immediately” supply 300,000 tons of diesel to the U.S. and global markets, followed by another 500,000 metric tons in November and 1 million metric tons thereafter. The deal comes as U.S. diesel prices have risen to $6.179 per gallon, up nearly 70% year-on-year, amid the turmoil that has gripped the global oil market since the start of the Iran war in late February. text: St. Petersburg Bans Migrant Workers From Gym, Hair Salon and Retail Work Oct. 16, 2026 Igor Ivanko / Moskva News Agency St. Petersburg authorities have banned foreign citizens with work patents from employment in retail, healthcare, beauty salons and fitness centers, local media reported Thursday. Governor Alexander Beglov’s decree expands on existing restrictions, which last year banned migrant patent holders — a temporary low-skilled work visa — from driving taxis and delivering food. Employers have been given until Dec. 15 to bring their staffing into compliance. The decision aims to combat “shadow employment” and reduce economic reliance on low-skilled foreign labor, according to local outlet Fontanka. According to St. Petersburg authorities, it will also facilitate “a transparent, regulated labor market where jobs are generated for Russian citizens, including young people and students.” The restrictions do not apply to highly qualified specialists, foreigners with work permits or citizens of Armenia, Belarus, Kazakhstan or Kyrgyzstan. text: Trump denies limiting Ukraine access to Starlink network Image source, Getty Images By Hafsa Khalil Published 16 October 2026 US President Donald Trump has denied limiting Ukraine's access to Starlink's sister internet network Starshield after it restricted drone speed, hampering Kyiv's ability to protect itself from Russian attacks. "It wasn't me and I don't think it was [Starlink owner] Elon [Musk]," Trump said, hours after Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said the usual speed had yet to be restored. title: US senators call for investigation into Ukraine's Starlink restrictions
text: US senators call for investigation into Ukraine's Starlink restrictions Image source, Getty Images Image caption, Democratic Party Senator Jeanne Shaheen has spearheaded the cross-party statement from several US senators By Jack Burgess Published 16 October 2026 A bipartisan group of US senators has signed a letter demanding an urgent investigation into disruptions to SpaceX's Starlink internet network in Ukraine. Starlink is a vital tool allowing Kyiv to guide drones to Russian targets and protect its own skies, but on Tuesday night Ukraine said it had unexpectedly restricted how fast drones could fly while maintaining internet connection. In the letter, sent to the US defence department inspector general, the senators express "grave concern" about reports of speed curbs between 12 and 14 October. Asked whether the US might have had a role in the slowdown, a US official told the BBC "no such request was ever made by the president [Donald Trump]". The letter, led by Jeanne Shaheen - a Democrat on the Senate's Foreign Relations Committee - calls for the inspector general to find out whether the restrictions were caused by the US defence department or its contractors. title: Russian Firms Stand to Gain Most From Trump’s Diesel Deal, Analysts Say
text: News Analysis Russian Firms Stand to Gain Most From Trump’s Diesel Deal, Analysts Say By Moscow Times Reporter Oct. 16, 2026 An employee holds a diesel fuel pump nozzle at a gas station in Moscow. REUTERS / Maxim Shemetov U.S. President Donald Trump’s diesel deal with Moscow could do more for Russian oil companies than for the American consumers he wants to help, analysts say. While Russian firms stand to benefit from looser export restrictions, the promised shipments may do little to bring down U.S. fuel prices. The agreement has drawn scathing criticism from Ukraine and its European allies, as well as scrutiny from lawmakers at home. But does it make economic sense? What does Trump want? Trump announced that Russia would “immediately” supply 300,000 tons of diesel to the U.S. and global markets, followed by another 500,000 metric tons in November and 1 million metric tons thereafter. The deal comes as U.S. diesel prices have risen to $6.179 per gallon, up nearly 70% year-on-year, amid the turmoil that has gripped the global oil market since the start of the Iran war in late February. title: Russian Courts Paralyzed by Yandex Cloud Outages After Drone Attacks – Vyorstka
text: Russian Courts Paralyzed by Yandex Cloud Outages After Drone Attacks – Vyorstka Oct. 16, 2026 Moskva News Agency Russian arbitration courts have been forced to postpone hearings and freeze legal filings following widespread system failures caused by Ukrainian drone attacks on Yandex data centers, exiled outlet Vyorstka reported Friday. The technical disruptions reportedly began on Oct. 8 after a Ukrainian drone attack damaged the first of three Yandex data centers in Russia. According to Vyorstka, the outages disabled online video hearings, froze official audio recordings and prevented judges from opening or downloading case files submitted by the parties. Judges were reportedly forced to put cases on hold, declare trial breaks or leave bankruptcy filings frozen. Court rulings directly cited server failures at Yandex Cloud as the reason for legal proceedings. “Difficulties operating the ‘Electronic Justice’ software package are observed on Oct. 14 due to a massive failure in the Yandex Cloud main data center,” states one judicial order by a regional court shared by the outlet. title: St. Petersburg Bans Migrant Workers From Gym, Hair Salon and Retail Work
text: St. Petersburg Bans Migrant Workers From Gym, Hair Salon and Retail Work Oct. 16, 2026 Igor Ivanko / Moskva News Agency St. Petersburg authorities have banned foreign citizens with work patents from employment in retail, healthcare, beauty salons and fitness centers, local media reported Thursday. Governor Alexander Beglov’s decree expands on existing restrictions, which last year banned migrant patent holders — a temporary low-skilled work visa — from driving taxis and delivering food. Employers have been given until Dec. 15 to bring their staffing into compliance. The decision aims to combat “shadow employment” and reduce economic reliance on low-skilled foreign labor, according to local outlet Fontanka. According to St. Petersburg authorities, it will also facilitate “a transparent, regulated labor market where jobs are generated for Russian citizens, including young people and students.” The restrictions do not apply to highly qualified specialists, foreigners with work permits or citizens of Armenia, Belarus, Kazakhstan or Kyrgyzstan. Citizens of other visa-free countries eligible to obtain a work patent in Russia include Azerbaijan, Moldova, Tajikistan and Uzbekistan. Dozens

title: Putin Vows Retribution for Attacks on Russian Data Centers While Downplaying Damage to Refineries
text: Putin Vows Retribution for Attacks on Russian Data Centers While Downplaying Damage to Refineries Oct. 16, 2026 Sputnik / Mikhail Metzel / Pool via REUTERS President Vladimir Putin warned Thursday that Russia is actively retaliating in response to recent Ukrainian attacks on its data centers, while simultaneously brushing off recent drone attacks on oil refineries. “They took the first step and we began to answer. Now they’re squealing over energy, as well as other facilities, including data centers. They started it. They shouldn’t have started it,” Putin said via video link at a business forum. “Before taking this step, they should have thought carefully about the consequences,” he told the Delovaya Rossiya association. His first public comments acknowledging drone attacks targeting Yandex and Sberbank data centers this month contradict the Russian Defense Ministry’s own reports that it began striking Ukrainian data centers last month. title: Ukrainian Drones Strike Energy Plant in Russia’s Largest Oil-Producing Region
text: Ukrainian Drones Strike Energy Plant in Russia’s Largest Oil-Producing Region Oct. 16, 2026 @exilenova_plus / Telegram A suspected Ukrainian drone attack sparked a fire at an industrial facility in western Siberia’s Khanty-Mansi autonomous district on Friday, local authorities said, in what appeared to be the first strike on energy infrastructure in Russia’s largest oil-producing region. Governor Ruslan Kukharuk said an “industrial facility in the Surgut district” caught fire following the attack. The extent of the damage was still being assessed. Residents identified the facility as the Surgut Condensate Stabilization Plant, according to the Ukrainian monitoring channel Supernova+ . Eyewitness footage shared by the channel showed a large fire sending thick black smoke into the sky. The plant, owned by Gazprom Pererabotka, is Russia’s largest facility for processing a mixture of crude oil and gas condensate, with a design capacity of 12 million metric tons per year. It produces gasoline, diesel, jet fuel, liquefied petroleum gas and stabilized gas condensate. Surgut lies around 2,500 kilometers (1,550 miles) from the Ukrainian border. title: Jailed Election Expert Kynev Denied Crutches After Leg Broken During Arrest, Journalist Says
text: Jailed Election Expert Kynev Denied Crutches After Leg Broken During Arrest, Journalist Says Oct. 16, 2026 Alexander Kynev. Vayvor Russian political scientist and election expert Alexander Kynev is unable to walk after being denied crutches at a Moscow detention center, a journalist who received a letter from him said. Kynev, who was arrested in late September on drug charges, has been transferred to Moscow’s Pre-Trial Detention Center No. 4, known as “Medved” (“Bear”), journalist Gleb Yarovoy said . His leg was reportedly broken during his arrest. “He writes that he is still in a cast and has about three more weeks to ‘walk’ around in it. Except he can’t walk,” Yarovoy wrote. Kynev also said he was being held in quarantine and receiving no information about the outside world, according to Yarovoy. Moscow’s Perovsky District Court ordered Kynev into pre-trial detention on Sept. 25 on charges of attempting to sell a large quantity of drugs. He denies wrongdoing and faces between 10 and 20 years in prison if convicted. title: Novaya Gazeta Editor-in-Chief Detained in Moscow
text: Novaya Gazeta Editor-in-Chief Detained in Moscow Oct. 16, 2026 Sergei Sokolov. @tvrain / X Russian law enforcement officers on Thursday raided the Moscow apartment of Sergei Sokolov, the editor-in-chief of independent newspaper Novaya Gazeta, before taking him in for questioning and subsequently releasing him. Novaya Gazeta said contact with Sokolov was initially lost at around noon Moscow time before he was scheduled to lead an editorial planning meeting. The publication said Sokolov was being transported to the Investigative Committee, Russia’s top investigative body, for questioning and that a lawyer was on their way to assist him. Sokolov was later released on Thursday evening after law enforcement questioned him, reportedly in connection with the case against Novaya Gazeta managing editor Oleg Roldugin. The raid on Sokolov’s apartment was conducted as part of an ongoing criminal investigation opened earlier this spring, law enforcement sources told the RBC outlet. Meanwhile, sources told the state-run news agency TASS that the investigation centered around the illegal use of personal information. text: Kremlin ‘Fully Agrees’ With Trump’s Zelensky Criticism Oct. 16, 2026 Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov. Sergei Vedyashkin / Moskva News Agency The Kremlin expressed “full” agreement Friday with U.S. President Donald Trump’s criticism of Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky over stalled peace efforts. “The fact that Zelensky doesn’t want to take responsibility and enter a peaceful settlement process is unambiguous,” Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov told reporters during a daily briefing. “Here, we fully agree with President Trump’s point of view,” Peskov said. title: Putin Hands Control of 5 Western Firms to Ukraine War Veteran
text: Putin Hands Control of 5 Western Firms to Ukraine War Veteran Oct. 16, 2026 Marat Mirkhaidarov. Social media President Vladimir Putin signed a decree Thursday placing the Russian assets of five major Western manufacturing companies under the temporary management of a little-known firm owned by an ex-official who fought in Ukraine. The targeted European and U.S. assets include French flooring giant Tarkett, Belgian hygiene manufacturer Ontex Ru, German plastic packager Menshen, corrugated producer Kappa Rus and metal packaging producer Eviosys, a subsidiary of the U.S. Sonoco Products Company. Their combined 2025 revenue exceeds 53 billion rubles ($633.2 million), with Tarkett accounting for 19.3 billion rubles, Kappa Rus 16.5 billion rubles, Ontex Ru 10.3 billion rubles, and Eviosys and Menshen 6.1 billion rubles and 1.4 billion rubles, respectively. Putin’s decree hands management rights to Tsentr Kapital Management Company, a Moscow entity established in February 2026, according to corporate registry data cited by RBC. Tsentr Kapital is owned by 47-year-old Marat Mirkhaidarov, the former deputy governor and chief of staff of Far East Russia’s Zabaikalsky region. Mirkhaidarov volu

text: Russia Repels 644 Ukrainian Drones as Trump Calls Attacks on Russian Refineries ‘Disgrace’ Oct. 16, 2026 Moscow Sheremetyevo Airport. title: Watch: BBC follows Ukraine's Operation Vivaldi pushing Russia back on frontline
text: Watch: BBC follows Ukraine's Operation Vivaldi pushing Russia back on frontline Watch: BBC follows Ukraine's Operation Vivaldi pushing Russia back on frontline Close Deep inside an underground bunker in eastern Ukraine, commanders monitor the battlefield through a live video feed as a Ukrainian drone intercepts a Russian surveillance drone. The footage shows the Ukrainian drone hovering above its target, before dropping a net and dragging it from the sky. The interception is part of Operation Vivaldi, a Ukrainian counter-offensive that Kyiv says has recaptured 277 sq km (106 square miles) of territory in the eastern Donbas region in recent months. But Ukraine says new restrictions on Starshield, the military version of Elon Musk's Starlink satellite network, are threatening its drone operations. The technology has played a key role in helping Ukrainian forces detect and strike Russian targets. Dan Johnson reports from the bunker. Read more about Ukraine's counter-offensive. REUTERS / Maxim Shemetov U.S. President Donald Trump’s diesel deal with Moscow could do more for Russian oil companies than for the American consumers he wants to help, analysts say. While Russian firms stand to benefit from looser export restrictions, the promised shipments may do little to bring down U.S. fuel prices. Trump announced that Russia would “immediately” supply 300,000 tons of diesel to the U.S. and global markets, followed by another 500,000 metric tons in November and 1 million metric tons thereafter. The deal comes as U.S. diesel prices have risen to $6.179 per gallon, up nearly 70% year-on-year, amid the turmoil that has gripped the global oil market since the start of the Iran war in late February. title: St. Petersburg Bans Migrant Workers From Gym, Hair Salon and Retail Work
text: St. Petersburg Bans Migrant Workers From Gym, Hair Salon and Retail Work Oct. 16, 2026 Igor Ivanko / Moskva News Agency St. Petersburg authorities have banned foreign citizens with work patents from employment in retail, healthcare, beauty salons and fitness centers, local media reported Thursday. Governor Alexander Beglov’s decree expands on existing restrictions, which last year banned migrant patent holders — a temporary low-skilled work visa — from driving taxis and delivering food. Employers have been given until Dec. 15 to bring their staffing into compliance. The decision aims to combat “shadow employment” and reduce economic reliance on low-skilled foreign labor, according to local outlet Fontanka. According to St. Petersburg authorities, it will also facilitate “a transparent, regulated labor market where jobs are generated for Russian citizens, including young people and students.” The restrictions do not apply to highly qualified specialists, foreigners with work permits or citizens of Armenia, Belarus, Kazakhstan or Kyrgyzstan. title: Ukrainian Drones Strike Energy Plant in Russia’s Largest Oil-Producing Region
text: Ukrainian Drones Strike Energy Plant in Russia’s Largest Oil-Producing Region Oct. 16, 2026 @exilenova_plus / Telegram A suspected Ukrainian drone attack sparked a fire at an industrial facility in western Siberia’s Khanty-Mansi autonomous district on Friday, local authorities said, in what appeared to be the first strike on energy infrastructure in Russia’s largest oil-producing region. Governor Ruslan Kukharuk said an “industrial facility in the Surgut district” caught fire following the attack. The extent of the damage was still being assessed. Residents identified the facility as the Surgut Condensate Stabilization Plant, according to the Ukrainian monitoring channel Supernova+ . Eyewitness footage shared by the channel showed a large fire sending thick black smoke into the sky. The plant, owned by Gazprom Pererabotka, is Russia’s largest facility for processing a mixture of crude oil and gas condensate, with a design capacity of 12 million metric tons per year. It produces gasoline, diesel, jet fuel, liquefied petroleum gas and stabilized gas condensate. Surgut lies around 2,500 kilometers (1,550 miles) from the Ukrainian border. text: Jailed Election Expert Kynev Denied Crutches After Leg Broken During Arrest, Journalist Says Oct. 16, 2026 Alexander Kynev. Vayvor Russian political scientist and election expert Alexander Kynev is unable to walk after being denied crutches at a Moscow detention center, a journalist who received a letter from him said. Kynev, who was arrested in late September on drug charges, has been transferred to Moscow’s Pre-Trial Detention Center No. 4, known as “Medved” (“Bear”), journalist Gleb Yarovoy said . His leg was reportedly broken during his arrest. “He writes that he is still in a cast and has about three more weeks to ‘walk’ around in it. Except he can’t walk,” Yarovoy wrote. Kynev also said he was being held in quarantine and receiving no information about the outside world, according to Yarovoy. Moscow’s Perovsky District Court ordered Kynev into pre-trial detention on Sept. 25 on charges of attempting to sell a large quantity of drugs. He denies wrongdoing and faces between 10 and 20 years in prison if convicted. text: Novaya Gazeta Editor-in-Chief Detained in Moscow Oct. 16, 2026 Sergei Sokolov. @tvrain / X Russian law enforcement officers on Thursday raided the Moscow apartment of Sergei Sokolov, the editor-in-chief of independent newspaper Novaya Gazeta, before taking him in for questioning and subsequently releasing him. Novaya Gazeta said contact with Sokolov was initially lost at around noon Moscow time before he was scheduled to lead an editorial planning meeting. The publication said Sokolov was being transported to the Investigative Committee, Russia’s top investigative body, for questioning and that a lawyer was on their way to assist him. Sokolov was later released on Thursday evening after law enforcement questioned him, reportedly in connection with the case against Novaya Gazeta managing editor Oleg Roldugin. title: Putin Hands Control of 5 Western Firms to Ukraine War Veteran
text: Putin Hands Control of 5 Western Firms to Ukraine War Veteran Oct. 16, 2026 Marat Mirkhaidarov. Social media President Vladimir Putin signed a decree Thursday placing the Russian assets of five major Western manufacturing companies under the temporary management of a little-known firm owned by an ex-official who fought in Ukraine. The targeted European and U.S. assets include French flooring giant Tarkett, Belgian hygiene manufacturer Ontex Ru, German plastic packager Menshen, corrugated producer Kappa Rus and metal packaging producer Eviosys, a subsidiary of the U.S. Sonoco Products Company. Their combined 2025 revenue exceeds 53 billion rubles ($633.2 million), with Tarkett accounting for 19.3 billion rubles, Kappa Rus 16.5 billion rubles, Ontex Ru 10.3 billion rubles, and Eviosys and Menshen 6.1 billion rubles and 1.4 billion rubles, respectively. Putin’s decree hands management rights to Tsentr Kapital Management Company, a Moscow entity established in February 2026, according to corporate registry data cited by RBC. text: Russia Repels 644 Ukrainian Drones as Trump Calls Attacks on Russian Refineries ‘Disgrace’ Oct. 16, 2026 Moscow Sheremetyevo Airport. title: St. Petersburg Bans Migrant Workers From Gym, Hair Salon and Retail Work
text: St. Petersburg Bans Migrant Workers From Gym, Hair Salon and Retail Work Oct. 16, 2026 Igor Ivanko / Moskva News Agency St. Petersburg authorities have banned foreign citizens with work patents from employment in retail, healthcare, beauty salons and fitness centers, local media reported Thursday. Governor Alexander Beglov’s decree expands on existing restrictions, which last year banned migrant patent holders — a temporary low-skilled work visa — from driving taxis and delivering food. Employers have been given until Dec. 15 to bring their staffing into compliance. The decision aims to combat “shadow employment” and reduce economic reliance on low-skilled foreign labor, according to local outlet Fontanka. text: Jailed Election Expert Kynev Denied Crutches After Leg Broken During Arrest, Journalist Says Oct. 16, 2026 Alexander Kynev. Kynev, who was arrested in late September on drug charges, has been transferred to Moscow’s Pre-Trial Detention Center No. 4, known as “Medved” (“Bear”), journalist Gleb Yarovoy said . His leg was reportedly broken during his arrest. “He writes that he is still in a cast and has about three more weeks to ‘walk’ around in it. Except he can’t walk,” Yarovoy wrote. title: Putin Hands Control of 5 Western Firms to Ukraine War Veteran
text: Putin Hands Control of 5 Western Firms to Ukraine War Veteran Oct. 16, 2026 Marat Mirkhaidarov. Social media President Vladimir Putin signed a decree Thursday placing the Russian assets of five major Western manufacturing companies under the temporary management of a little-known firm owned by an ex-official who fought in Ukraine. The targeted European and U.S. assets include French flooring giant Tarkett, Belgian hygiene manufacturer Ontex Ru, German plastic packager Menshen, corrugated producer Kappa Rus and metal packaging producer Eviosys, a subsidiary of the U.S. Sonoco Products Company. Their combined 2025 revenue exceeds 53 billion rubles ($633.2 million), with Tarkett accounting for 19.3 billion rubles, Kappa Rus 16.5 billion rubles, Ontex Ru 10.3 billion rubles, and Eviosys and Menshen 6.1 billion rubles and 1.4 billion rubles, respectively. text: Watch: BBC follows Ukraine's Operation Vivaldi pushing Russia back on frontline Watch: BBC follows Ukraine's Operation Vivaldi pushing Russia back on frontline Close Deep inside an underground bunker in eastern Ukraine, commanders monitor the battlefield through a live video feed as a Ukrainian drone intercepts a Russian surveillance drone. The interception is part of Operation Vivaldi, a Ukrainian counter-offensive that Kyiv says has recaptured 277 sq km (106 square miles) of territory in the eastern Donbas region in recent months. title: St. Petersburg Bans Migrant Workers From Gym, Hair Salon and Retail Work
text: St. Petersburg Bans Migrant Workers From Gym, Hair Salon and Retail Work Oct. 16, 2026 Igor Ivanko / Moskva News Agency St. Petersburg authorities have banned foreign citizens with work patents from employment in retail, healthcare, beauty salons and fitness centers, local media reported Thursday. Governor Alexander Beglov’s decree expands on existing restrictions, which last year banned migrant patent holders — a temporary low-skilled work visa — from driving taxis and delivering food. Employers have been given until Dec. 15 to bring their staffing into compliance. The decision aims to combat “shadow employment” and reduce economic reliance on low-skilled foreign labor, according to local outlet Fontanka. According to St. Petersburg authorities, it will also facilitate “a transparent, regulated labor market where jobs are generated for Russian citizens, including young people and students.” The restrictions do not apply to highly qualified specialists, foreigners with work permits or citizens of Armenia, Belarus, Kazakhstan or Kyrgyzstan. text: St. Petersburg Bans Migrant Workers From Gym, Hair Salon and Retail Work Oct. 16, 2026 Igor Ivanko / Moskva News Agency St. Petersburg authorities have banned foreign citizens with work patents from employment in retail, healthcare, beauty salons and fitness centers, local media reported Thursday. Governor Ruslan Kukharuk said an “industrial facility in the Surgut district” caught fire following the attack. The extent of the damage was still being assessed. text: Putin Hands Control of 5 Western Firms to Ukraine War Veteran Oct. 16, 2026 Marat Mirkhaidarov. Social media President Vladimir Putin signed a decree Thursday placing the Russian assets of five major Western manufacturing companies under the temporary management of a little-known firm owned by an ex-official who fought in Ukraine. title: Trump denies limiting Ukraine access to Starlink network
text: Trump denies limiting Ukraine access to Starlink network Image source, Getty Images By Hafsa Khalil Published 16 October 2026 US President Donald Trump has denied limiting Ukraine's access to Starlink's sister internet network Starshield after it restricted drone speed, hampering Kyiv's ability to protect itself from Russian attacks. "It wasn't me and I don't think it was [Starlink owner] Elon [Musk]," Trump said, hours after Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said the usual speed had yet to be restored. Musk himself suggested the US government might have been behind the restrictions, while news agency Reuters reported on Thursday that the order had come from inside the White House. Ukraine was hit by several deadly strikes on Tuesday after the network slowdown. Starlink is a civilian-use, high-speed internet network operated by Musk's SpaceX. Starshield - which relies on Starlink - is its military-grade counterpart that was designed for the Pentagon. The US had previously warned it could withhold sharing intelligence, crucial for Kyiv's defences, if Ukraine did not stop hitting Russian oil refineries. title: Watch: BBC follows Ukraine's Operation Vivaldi pushing Russia back on frontline
text: Watch: BBC follows Ukraine's Operation Vivaldi pushing Russia back on frontline Watch: BBC follows Ukraine's Operation Vivaldi pushing Russia back on frontline Close Deep inside an underground bunker in eastern Ukraine, commanders monitor the battlefield through a live video feed as a Ukrainian drone intercepts a Russian surveillance drone. The footage shows the Ukrainian drone hovering above its target, before dropping a net and dragging it from the sky. The interception is part of Operation Vivaldi, a Ukrainian counter-offensive that Kyiv says has recaptured 277 sq km (106 square miles) of territory in the eastern Donbas region in recent months. But Ukraine says new restrictions on Starshield, the military version of Elon Musk's Starlink satellite network, are threatening its drone operations. The technology has played a key role in helping Ukrainian forces detect and strike Russian targets. Dan Johnson reports from the bunker. Read more about Ukraine's counter-offensive. Employers have been given until Dec. 15 to bring their staffing into compliance. The decision aims to combat “shadow employment” and reduce economic reliance on low-skilled foreign labor, according to local outlet Fontanka. According to St. Petersburg authorities, it will also facilitate “a transparent, regulated labor market where jobs are generated for Russian citizens, including young people and students.” The restrictions do not apply to highly qualified specialists, foreigners with work permits or citizens of Armenia, Belarus, Kazakhstan or Kyrgyzstan. title: Putin Vows Retribution for Attacks on Russian Data Centers While Downplaying Damage to Refineries
text: Putin Vows Retribution for Attacks on Russian Data Centers While Downplaying Damage to Refineries Oct. 16, 2026 Sputnik / Mikhail Metzel / Pool via REUTERS President Vladimir Putin warned Thursday that Russia is actively retaliating in response to recent Ukrainian attacks on its data centers, while simultaneously brushing off recent drone attacks on oil refineries. “They took the first step and we began to answer. Now they’re squealing over energy, as well as other facilities, including data centers. They started it. They shouldn’t have started it,” Putin said via video link at a business forum. “Before taking this step, they should have thought carefully about the consequences,” he told the Delovaya Rossiya association. His first public comments acknowledging drone attacks targeting Yandex and Sberbank data centers this month contradict the Russian Defense Ministry’s own reports that it began striking Ukrainian data centers last month. title: Ukrainian Drones Strike Energy Plant in Russia’s Largest Oil-Producing Region
text: Ukrainian Drones Strike Energy Plant in Russia’s Largest Oil-Producing Region Oct. 16, 2026 @exilenova_plus / Telegram A suspected Ukrainian drone attack sparked a fire at an industrial facility in western Siberia’s Khanty-Mansi autonomous district on Friday, local authorities said, in what appeared to be the first strike on energy infrastructure in Russia’s largest oil-producing region. Governor Ruslan Kukharuk said an “industrial facility in the Surgut district” caught fire following the attack. The extent of the damage was still being assessed. Residents identified the facility as the Surgut Condensate Stabilization Plant, according to the Ukrainian monitoring channel Supernova+ . Eyewitness footage shared by the channel showed a large fire sending thick black smoke into the sky. The plant, owned by Gazprom Pererabotka, is Russia’s largest facility for processing a mixture of crude oil and gas condensate, with a design capacity of 12 million metric tons per year. It produces gasoline, diesel, jet fuel, liquefied petroleum gas and stabilized gas condensate. Surgut lies around 2,500 kilometers (1,550 miles) from the Ukrainian border. title: Jailed Election Expert Kynev Denied Crutches After Leg Broken During Arrest, Journalist Says
text: Jailed Election Expert Kynev Denied Crutches After Leg Broken During Arrest, Journalist Says Oct. 16, 2026 Alexander Kynev. Vayvor Russian political scientist and election expert Alexander Kynev is unable to walk after being denied crutches at a Moscow detention center, a journalist who received a letter from him said. Kynev, who was arrested in late September on drug charges, has been transferred to Moscow’s Pre-Trial Detention Center No. 4, known as “Medved” (“Bear”), journalist Gleb Yarovoy said . His leg was reportedly broken during his arrest. “He writes that he is still in a cast and has about three more weeks to ‘walk’ around in it. Except he can’t walk,” Yarovoy wrote. Kynev also said he was being held in quarantine and receiving no information about the outside world, according to Yarovoy. Moscow’s Perovsky District Court ordered Kynev into pre-trial detention on Sept. 25 on charges of attempting to sell a large quantity of drugs. He denies wrongdoing and faces between 10 and 20 years in prison if convicted. title: Novaya Gazeta Editor-in-Chief Detained in Moscow
text: Novaya Gazeta Editor-in-Chief Detained in Moscow Oct. 16, 2026 Sergei Sokolov. @tvrain / X Russian law enforcement officers on Thursday raided the Moscow apartment of Sergei Sokolov, the editor-in-chief of independent newspaper Novaya Gazeta, before taking him in for questioning and subsequently releasing him. Novaya Gazeta said contact with Sokolov was initially lost at around noon Moscow time before he was scheduled to lead an editorial planning meeting. The publication said Sokolov was being transported to the Investigative Committee, Russia’s top investigative body, for questioning and that a lawyer was on their way to assist him. Sokolov was later released on Thursday evening after law enforcement questioned him, reportedly in connection with the case against Novaya Gazeta managing editor Oleg Roldugin. The raid on Sokolov’s apartment was conducted as part of an ongoing criminal investigation opened earlier this spring, law enforcement sources told the RBC outlet. Meanwhile, sources told the state-run news agency TASS that the investigation centered around the illegal use of personal information. title: Kremlin ‘Fully Agrees’ With Trump’s Zelensky Criticism
text: Kremlin ‘Fully Agrees’ With Trump’s Zelensky Criticism Oct. 16, 2026 Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov. Sergei Vedyashkin / Moskva News Agency The Kremlin expressed “full” agreement Friday with U.S. President Donald Trump’s criticism of Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky over stalled peace efforts. “The fact that Zelensky doesn’t want to take responsibility and enter a peaceful settlement process is unambiguous,” Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov told reporters during a daily briefing. “Here, we fully agree with President Trump’s point of view,” Peskov said. Trump sharply criticized Zelensky in an interview with the Newsmax outlet, saying he believes Russia and Ukraine will end up reaching a ceasefire after the Ukrainian leader steps down. “He doesn’t want to settle. He says he wants to settle, but he doesn’t,” Trump said of Zelensky and the conflict running for more than four and a half years. title: Putin Hands Control of 5 Western Firms to Ukraine War Veteran
text: Putin Hands Control of 5 Western Firms to Ukraine War Veteran Oct. 16, 2026 Marat Mirkhaidarov. Social media President Vladimir Putin signed a decree Thursday placing the Russian assets of five major Western manufacturing companies under the temporary management of a little-known firm owned by an ex-official who fought in Ukraine. The targeted European and U.S. assets include French flooring giant Tarkett, Belgian hygiene manufacturer Ontex Ru, German plastic packager Menshen, corrugated producer Kappa Rus and metal packaging producer Eviosys, a subsidiary of the U.S. Sonoco Products Company. Their combined 2025 revenue exceeds 53 billion rubles ($633.2 million), with Tarkett accounting for 19.3 billion rubles, Kappa Rus 16.5 billion rubles, Ontex Ru 10.3 billion rubles, and Eviosys and Menshen 6.1 billion rubles and 1.4 billion rubles, respectively. Putin’s decree hands management rights to Tsentr Kapital Management Company, a Moscow entity established in February 2026, according to corporate registry data cited by RBC. title: Russia Repels 644 Ukrainian Drones as Trump Calls Attacks on Russian Refineries ‘Disgrace’
text: Russia Repels 644 Ukrainian Drones as Trump Calls Attacks on Russian Refineries ‘Disgrace’ Oct. 16, 2026 Moscow Sheremetyevo Airport. Yaroslav Chingaev / Moskva News Agency Russia’s Defense Ministry said Friday that 644 Ukrainian drones were intercepted over 26 Russian regions and annexed Crimea overnight, as U.S. President Donald Trump called Ukrainian attacks on Russian refineries a “disgrace.” Vladimir region Governor Alexander Avdeyev said air defenses repelled an attack aimed at municipal heating infrastructure serving the regional capital. According to Avdeyev, there were “minor” damages. Unverified reporting by monitoring channels that shared video of an explosion against the dark sky claimed it targeted a data center owned by tech giant Yandex in Vladimir, which was previously damaged in last weekend’s strike. Moscow Mayor Sergei Sobyanin said air defenses shot down 94 Ukrainian drones on approach to the capital between Thursday evening and Friday morning. Nearly 160 flights were delayed or canceled across Moscow’s four main airports, with Sheremetyevo and Vnukovo bearing the brunt.
